hits.definition: Floors, dust, dishes, laundry and rooms clean themselves or are cleaned by built-in machinery without human work.

hits.title: Anticipations

awards.title: The Long View

hits.event: About 20 Rheinbote four-stage rockets were fired from Zwolle in the Netherlands against Antwerp, starting in autumn 1944 (Wikipedia gives December 1944 to January 1945; a 1948 BIS article says November 1944).

hits.definition: A device worn to amplify faint sounds or shift them into the audible range so a person can hear better.

hits.title: New Atlantis

hits.definition: An additional small natural satellite of Earth besides the Moon, previously undiscovered or newly captured, is found orbiting the planet.

hits.event: Catalina Sky Survey (Arizona) discovered 6R10DB9, later 2006 RH120, a meter-size natural object captured into Earth orbit and making repeated loops until mid-2007.

hits.concept: Phobos and Deimos, the two moons of Mars

hits.event: Asaph Hall at the U.S. Naval Observatory found Deimos (first seen 11 Aug 1877) and Phobos (17-18 Aug) with the 26-inch refractor; the discovery was telegraphed on 19 Aug

hits.definition: A spacecraft or station sits at a point between two worlds, such as Earth and Moon, where their gravitational pulls balance so it stays in place relative to them.

hits.title: All Around the Moon
hits.event: ISEE-3 in its L1 halo orbit began measuring the solar wind upstream of Earth, the station role later filled operationally by SOHO, Wind and DSCOVR.

hits.concept: Hydrogen and oxygen engines and heating
hits.definition: Burning hydrogen with oxygen in engines, furnaces or turbines to give motive power, heat or electricity.

hits.definition: A sealed suit with its own air supply and communication that lets a person survive and work outside a spacecraft or on another world.

hits.event: Yevgeny Khrunov and Alexei Yeliseyev, wearing Yastreb suits with chest-mounted regenerative life-support units, spacewalked from Soyuz 5 to Soyuz 4 to transfer crews between two docked spacecraft.

hits.concept: Walking and leaping in low gravity
hits.definition: On the Moon or small bodies, reduced gravity lets people take huge bounds and carry loads easily.
hits.quote: you can take a stride 15 feet in width as easily as you can now take one of ordinary length.
hits.title: All Around the Moon
hits.event: The same Apollo 11 moonwalk was real exploration work: the crew loped about the surface, set up experiments and collected samples, with loping becoming their preferred way to move.

hits.definition: A powered, fixed-wing heavier-than-air flying machine that carries a pilot or passengers under control.

hits.event: Philip Parmalee flew a Wright biplane from Dayton to Columbus, Ohio, carrying bolts of silk for a department store, the first commercial cargo flight (about 62 miles in under an hour).

hits.definition: A huge gun able to shell targets scores of miles or leagues away.

hits.concept: Nature and observation of the solar corona
hits.definition: An explanation of the Sun's corona as radiation-driven particles or gas, and how it can be observed outside a total eclipse.
hits.quote: Although many attempts have been made to render the corona visible when there is no eclipse, all have failed, and it is to the moon alone that we owe its revelation.
hits.title: Curiosities of the Sky
hits.event: The Harvard High Altitude Observatory at Climax, Colorado opened 8 September 1940 with a Lyot-type coronagraph and obtained daily records of the corona's spectrum as an index of solar activity.

hits.definition: A man-made object placed in orbit around the Earth that stays up and circles it, including relay and communication satellites.
